method: A DCP is a delivery container rather than a video file: the picture is a JPEG 2000 track of whole frames in CIE XYZ at 12 bits per component, the sound is uncompressed 24-bit PCM, and both are wrapped in MXF beside a composition playlist and a packing list. The page budgets that package from its runtime, container, active picture, frame rate, image bit rate, audio channels, sample rate and delivery drive. The container is 2048 x 1080 (2K) or 4096 x 2160 (4K); the active picture is flat at 1998 x 1080 or 3996 x 2160, scope at 2048 x 858 or 4096 x 1716, HDTV at 1920 x 1080 or 3840 x 2160, or the full container, and the page reports the pillarbox or letterbox bars around it. The frame count is the runtime times the frame rate, the frame budget is the image bit rate divided by 8 and by the frame rate, and the picture track is the frame count times that budget. The sound track is channels x sample rate x 3 bytes for the presentation time, so 5.1 at 48 kHz costs 6.912 Mbit/s. A 1% allowance covers the MXF wrapping, the playlist, the packing list and their hashes; subtitles, encryption, closed captions and the reel splits of a long feature are not modelled, and every size is a decimal gigabyte because drives are sold that way. The DCI limits drive the refusals: the image essence is capped at 250 Mbit/s, a 4K container carries 24, 25 or 30 fps while a 2K container carries 24, 25, 30, 48, 50 or 60, and a stereoscopic package is 2K at 24 or 48 fps with both eyes sharing the 250 Mbit/s, so each eye is budgeted at half the entered rate. Frame rates are whole numbers, because a DCP counts frames rather than following a 23.976 timeline, and the runtime is limited to 8 hours. The result is the encoder's target, not a measurement: JPEG 2000 is variable rate, so the finished picture track lands near the budget, and an encrypted or subtitled package is slightly larger.

sources.title: Digital Cinema Package - a DCP carries JPEG 2000 picture essence and 24-bit linear PCM sound, allows 24, 25, 30, 48, 50 and 60 fps at 2K and 24, 25 and 30 fps at 4K, places flat 1998 x 1080 or 3996 x 2160 and scope 2048 x 858 or 4096 x 1716 pictures in 2048 x 1080 or 4096 x 2160 containers, and caps the picture at 250 Mbit/s shared by both eyes of a stereoscopic package

Digital cinema - the DCI specification encodes picture as JPEG 2000 in CIE XYZ at 12 bits per component, supports 2K at 24 or 48 fps and 4K at 24 fps, and carries up to 16 channels of 24-bit uncompressed audio at 48 kHz or 96 kHz
